This file, VK_VIDEO_std_h264.xml, gives the Venus protocol generator field-level definitions for the StdVideo H.264 decode types.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
vk.xml declares these types by name only, because they are defined in the Khronos video headers rather than in the Vulkan registry:
<type requires="vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_h264std_decode.h" name="StdVideoDecodeH264PictureInfo"/>
With no members, Gen.is_serializable() rejects them, and _init_supported_types() then filters every struct that points at them out of the pNext chains. The effect is silent: generation succeeds and the video commands look complete, but the codec payload never crosses the wire.
Describing the members here lets the existing generator emit field-level encode/decode/size functions, so there is no hand-written serialization to review and no path by which a raw struct copy could creep in.
BITFIELDS ARE NOT DESCRIBED HERE
The StdVideo *Flags types are C bitfields. They are deliberately NOT expressed as members, because the generator's scalar helpers take pointers (vn_encode_uint32_t(enc, const uint32_t *val)) and taking the address of a bitfield is illegal C. Describing them as one opaque uint32_t and copying it would compile but would depend on implementation-defined bitfield allocation order, which guest and host are not guaranteed to agree on.
Instead each *Flags struct is carried as a single uint32_t whose bit assignments are fixed by explicit shifts over named fields in vn_protocol_video_h264_flags.h. The shift assignments are part of the wire contract: reordering them silently corrupts decode parameters.

types.comment: Array extents, mirroring the STD_VIDEO_* macros in vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_h264std{,_decode}.h. These bound every array below, so a guest cannot describe an oversized list.
